Three simple diagrams side-by-side. 1. A straight horizontal line with a diagonal line cutting it, creating angles a and b. A central point with four rays coming out, creating angles p, q, r, s. Label: p + q + r + s = 360°. 3. Two straight lines forming an X shape, with top/bottom angles labelled x and x, and left/right angles labelled y and y. Label: Vertically opposite angles are equal. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Three circles side-by-side illustrating the first three theorems. 1. A circle with an arc AB. Lines go from A and B to the centre O (angle 2x) and from A and B to a point P on the circumference (angle x). 2. A circle with a chord CD. Lines go from C and D to two different points P and Q on the same side of the circumference. Both angles at P and Q are labelled $\theta$. 3. A circle with diameter XY passing through centre O. Lines go from X and Y to a point Z on the circumference. The angle at Z has a square right-angle symbol.

A circle illustrating the alternate segment theorem. A tangent line touches the circle at point P. A triangle PQR is drawn inside the circle. The angle between the tangent and chord PQ is labelled $x$. The angle at the opposite vertex R is also labelled $x$.

Two horizontal parallel lines cut by a diagonal transversal line. Eight angles are formed, labelled 1 to 8. Angles 1, 4, 5, 8 are highlighted in one colour (equal angles), and angles 2, 3, 6, 7 in another colour (equal angles). Labels to indicate corresponding pairs (e.g., 1 and 5), alternate pairs (e.g., 4 and 5), and co-interior pairs (e.g., 4 and 6, which sum to 180°).

A construction of a 75° angle. A horizontal line AB with a point O. An initial large arc from the baseline. An intersection for 60°, an intersection for 120°, and intersecting arcs above them for a 90° dotted vertical line. Another set of intersecting arcs bisecting the space between the 60° line and the 90° line. A solid final line passes through this last intersection, labelled as 75°.
